results.summary:
`hkb serve` now holds several checkouts on one server, one port and one page (read side only; the dispatcher keeps its own card).

Selection: `--repos ../a,../b#board` adds checkouts to the one you ran in, or list them once in ~/.config/hkb/boards.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/$KB_CONFIG_HOME honoured). Nothing is scanned for. A bad --repos path is fatal; a stale entry in the user list is a warning and a skip.

Addressing: every board gets a URL-safe `owner~repo~slug` key (src/model.js boardKey/uniqueKeys) and its own closure — cache, in-flight read, generation, detail map. dispatcherState, logPathFor and every verb resolve against that board ctx. New route /api/boards/<key>/tasks/<n>[/<verb>]; the unscoped /api/tasks/<n> still resolves when there is exactly one board and is a 400 naming the keys when there are more (an unknown key is a 404 listing the keys).

Page: still one inline file, seven columns, and identical with one board. With more, a board bar appears (chip per board with its own dispatcher dot + count, click to filter) and each card carries its repo. The board key travels with the card via data-card="<key>#<n>" into dataTransfer, so a drag can only act on the repo it came from. /api/board now returns { columns, poll, host, fetched_at, boards: [...] } — a shape change on a page-private endpoint.

Isolation: a board that fails to read keeps its last good cards, reports error/stale, is cached like a success, and shows in an error strip; the other boards render normally (previously one bad read failed the page).

Frugality unchanged: one GraphQL query per board per poll on the same conditional-read/304 path, no new dependency, no build step.

Next worker: if you add a cross-repo dispatcher (the sibling card), serveContexts/keyBoards in src/serve.js are the reusable half — they resolve paths to contexts and key them; only the accounting of max_in_progress and the daily spawn cap is still open.
